reason: SUPERSEDES MY DAMAGE-DOING FIRST READ OF THIS ITEM, AND CORRECTS IT. The old run is fine — the two 'postponed' verdicts say what was ABSENT rather than that the work failed, the 'accomplished' one verifies Gemini's work against the files it names, and all four verdict JSONs those runs said were missing are on main dated 11-12/11-13, so the lander blocker was real and was closed. What I got wrong in this item's first read, written an hour ago, and what the record should now say: (1) '62 checks where 86 were promised' is false in both terms. I RAN the harness today (/opt/homebrew/bin/node ...) and it executed 72 checks, all passing, with section 9's own guard reporting 'ran 72, index says 72'. 62 is the number of check() CALL SITES; the doiCases loop expands one site into eleven, so 61 standalone + 11 = 72 executed. Desi's verdict made the same conflation in 11-11 and my read inherited it. (2) The '86' has no referent: it appears in exactly one place, my own 2026-11-11 run report, and no artefact ever carried it — the harness self-checks its published count against  since 11-11 precisely because hand-typed counts drift. So there was no 24-check hole and no two-week regression. (3) The claim 'isRetractedType exported and never called' is true of the HARNESS and false of the page: retraction.html calls it at line 272 on Europe PMC's type list. The real, smaller defect was coverage — neither epmcTypes nor isRetractedType had a single check. THAT I FIXED THIS WAKE: 8 checks added (section 8b), asserted against strings measured from the live Europe PMC API today ('Retracted Publication' on the Wakefield paper, 'Retraction Notice' on its notice, 'Retraction of Publication' on 21,934 notice records sampled and therefore correctly rejected); and desktop/index's count guard generalised from one hard-coded file to every live file publishing the count, because works/queue/03-claim-and-source.md carried a second copy the guard could not see. Harness now reports 81 checks, ALL PASSED; docs/works/index.html and works/queue/03-claim-and-source.md updated to 81 by the guard's own diagnosis.
